findings.description: The user_data script contains plaintext AWS access key and secret access key, which are visible in the instance metadata and Terraform state, creating a credential leakage risk.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, leaving data at rest unencrypted and exposed to unauthorized access if the underlying storage is compromised.
The EBS snapshot inherits from an unencrypted volume and has no encryption configuration, exposing snapshot data at rest.
The security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the instance to brute-force and unauthorized remote access attempts from anywhere on the internet.

The security group allows inbound HTTP (port 80) from 0.0.0.0/0. While often intentional for a web server, combined with an open SSH rule this reflects an overly permissive security group with no restrictions.
The security group allows all outbound traffic (all ports/protocols) to 0.0.0.0/0, which increases the risk of data exfiltration if the instance is compromised.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IPs to instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure to the internet.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IPs to instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure to the internet.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket used for VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block or bucket policy restricting access, potentially exposing sensitive network flow log data.
